encounters.cc: Regular contractions occurring every 5 minutes for the past two hours with bloody show

lines: Regular contractions occurring every 5 minutes for the past two hours with bloody show
She reports the contractions as moderately painful and notes the passage of a small amount of mucoid, blood-tinged vaginal discharge.
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and prenatal care has been adequate with no significant findings.
The patient inquires about the significance of the bloody show and the next steps in her management.
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 88 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, and temperature 98.6°F (37°C)
Fetal heart tracing is reassuring with a baseline of 140 bpm, moderate variability, no decelerations, and occasional accelerations.
A sterile speculum examination confirms the presence of bloody show without active bleeding.
Cervical examination reveals 4 cm dilation and 80% effacement.

encounters.cc: Perineal pain and difficulty with urination 5 days after first vaginal delivery

lines: Perineal pain and difficulty with urination 5 days after first vaginal delivery
The patient with primary adrenal insufficiency and diastasis recti abdominis returns for follow-up 5 days after vaginal delivery of her first child.
The delivery was complicated by a second-degree perineal laceration, which was repaired immediately postpartum.
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
She is breastfeeding and wishes to avoid medications that could affect her infant.
She denies fever, chills, or purulent discharge from the perineal area.
On examination, the perineum is edematous with mild erythema but without fluctuance or wound dehiscence.

encounters.cc: Persistent bilateral nipple pain and abrasions while breastfeeding 1-month-old infant

lines: Persistent bilateral nipple pain and abrasions while breastfeeding 1-month-old infant
The patient is a 30-year-old female with primary adrenal insufficiency and diastasis recti abdominis who returns approximately one month following normal spontaneous vaginal delivery.
She presents with persistent breastfeeding difficulties.
She describes the pain as sharp and burning, which worsens during feeding.
She also reports bilateral nipple abrasions and occasional bloody nipple discharge.
The patient has been exclusively breastfeeding and has not introduced bottle feeding.
The patient is concerned about the possibility of infection or underlying breast pathology.
Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she had a normal spontaneous vaginal delivery.
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
She denies any fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms.
On physical examination, the nipples are erythematous with small cracks, but there is no evidence of mastitis or breast engorgement.
No masses are palpable, and the infant appears well-nourished and active.

encounters.cc: 6 weeks postpartum with progressive fatigue, dizziness, 5kg weight loss, and skin hyperpigmentation

lines: 6 weeks postpartum with progressive fatigue, dizziness, 5kg weight loss, and skin hyperpigmentation
The patient presents 6 weeks postpartum after vaginal delivery.
She reports that her skin has become darker, especially in creases, scars, and her gums.
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, and she has orthostatic hypotension.

encounters.cc: Fever, malaise, and painful erythematous right breast for 4 days while breastfeeding

lines: Fever, malaise, and painful erythematous right breast for 4 days while breastfeeding
This 30-year-old female, 6 weeks postpartum with primary adrenal insufficiency, presents with acute breast symptoms.
She reports that the symptoms began with flu-like symptoms and localized breast pain during breastfeeding.
She was prescribed oral dicloxacillin 2 days ago but has not experienced any improvement.
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
She has no known drug allergies
On examination, her temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 88/min, and blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg.
The right breast has a 5 cm area of induration, warmth, and erythema in the upper outer quadrant without fluctuance.
There is no nipple discharge or retraction.
- Blood cultures: No growth to date

encounters.cc: 3-day history of increasing left breast pain, swelling, fever, and chills in breastfeeding mother

lines: 3-day history of increasing left breast pain, swelling, fever, and chills in breastfeeding mother

The patient is a 30-year-old female with primary adrenal insufficiency evaluated for right breast pain earlier today, and presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of increasing pain and swelling in her left breast.
She reports fever and chills since yesterday.
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg
The left breast is erythematous and edematous with a 5 cm fluctuant mass noted in the upper outer quadrant.
There is associated tenderness on palpation and axillary lymphadenopathy on the same side.

encounters.cc: Routine postpartum evaluation 24 hours after uncomplicated vaginal delivery of second child

lines: Routine postpartum evaluation 24 hours after uncomplicated vaginal delivery of second child

The patient with primary adrenal insufficiency returns for postpartum evaluation following her second vaginal delivery, three years after her first pregnancy was complicated by lactational breast abscess and adrenal insufficiency diagnosis.

She presents 24 hours after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a healthy full-term infant, reporting mild cramping and a small amount of vaginal bleeding described as less than her normal menstrual period.
She also mentions experiencing intermittent chills and shivering, but denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or headache.
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Her vital signs are as follows: temperature 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure 120/75 mmHg, heart rate 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute
Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender uterus just below the level of the umbilicus and mild lochia rubra without clots.
Her breasts are full and tender on palpation.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Postpartum check-up 8 weeks after second delivery with abdominal midline bulge

lines: Postpartum check-up 8 weeks after second delivery with abdominal midline bulge
The patient is a 33-year-old female with primary adrenal insufficiency who returns for routine postpartum care.
She gave birth to her second child 8 weeks ago via normal vaginal delivery.
She reports noticing a bulge in the midline of her abdomen that becomes more prominent when she is sitting up or when she strains.
She denies any pain associated with the bulge.
Her pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated.
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, a midline protrusion is noted above the umbilicus when she raises her head while lying down.
Palpation of the abdomen does not elicit tenderness, and the protrusion does not change with coughing.
There is no evidence of a hernia on examination.
